natural_body: Price-sensitive SMB 40% off: signups +31%, revenue +18%, retention -12%; renewals weak.

first.rationale: Activation is down 6% QoQ and onboarding completion down 4%, but memory_91 (activation messaging) and memory_31 (signup simplification) both showed durable improvements in early product adoption and first-week activation. Activation messaging is the most direct lever for the current symptom. Memory_86 showed that shortened onboarding improved time-to-value. Rather than pursuing promotional_pricing (memory_73 showed -12% retention risk and weak renewals, exactly the wrong signal given competitive pressure), I'm testing in-product activation messaging to re-engage the funnel. This preserves long-term unit economics while directly addressing the QoQ decline. Verifying memory_31 and memory_91 will confirm the effect sizes and methodology before rolling out. Referral_incentive (memory_57) is lower priority because it targets existing customers, not the current activation shortfall. Enterprise_sales_assist is orthogonal to the SMB activation problem. Promotional pricing risks the revenue quality objective and would likely compound retention issues under margin pressure.
